A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PaTaRM and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Content can be matched reliably, including experiments relocated from the appendix into the main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original reward-model evaluations, downstream RLHF experiments, robustness tests, ablations, and mathematical-reasoning results in Appendix G.3.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds Best-of-N evaluation, a pairwise-model noise comparison, and absolute-score tracking.

M1.justification: The PAR reward assignment, format penalties, dynamic rubric generation, and SFT-to-GRPO training pipeline are unchanged. The additional evaluations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v3 adds Best-of-N response-selection scenarios using GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3-4B candidates on AlpacaEval, MT-Bench, InfoBench, and IFEval. This extends coverage within existing conversational and instruction-following domains. GSM-8K and Math-500 were already evaluated in v2 Appendix G.3.

E2.justification: A standard pairwise GRM joins the label-noise comparison, and random selection provides a baseline in the new Best-of-N evaluation. BT-Qwen3 models are reused. Gemini Flash and Pro already appeared in v2's corresponding benchmark tables; their clearer naming does not add comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds a distinct controlled evaluation design: select among eight candidates sampled at temperature 1.0 with a 1024-token limit, compare matched-data BT-Qwen3 reward models, and use GPT-4.1 judgments with GPT-4.1-nano as the AlpacaEval reference. This substantially extends evaluation beyond the existing benchmark and policy-training protocols, which remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix G.3 tests whether noise robustness also holds for a standard pairwise GRM at 0%, 20%, and 50% label flips. G.4 supplements existing margin plots with absolute chosen/rejected score trajectories to investigate score inflation. These materially expand tests of competing explanations for PAR's behavior; earlier ablations and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean and standard deviation over four independent random-seed runs in Appendix G.1. The corresponding uncertainty values and reporting practice are unchanged, and the new experiments introduce no additional uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results in Tables 2, 17, and 18: Best-of-N outcomes, pairwise-GRM noise collapse, and absolute-score trajectories. For example, Table 2 reports AlpacaEval scores of 19.99 versus 14.66 for PaTaRM-8B and BT-Qwen3-8B with Qwen3-4B candidates. The Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct SFT IFEval average changes from 64.1 in v2 Table 17 to 74.1 in v3 Table 19. Existing main benchmark and mathematical-reasoning scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reward equations in Section 3.1 and ranking-complexity arguments in Appendix A are retained. The revised noise explanation adds no formal variance analysis, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly identifies base models and policies as the references for the retained 8.7% and 13.6% improvement claims. The third contribution now acknowledges BT's RewardBench advantage and adds a matched-data Best-of-N utility claim. The central PAR and adaptive-rubric contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 attributes recovery under 50% label noise to pretrained reasoning filtering incorrect labels. v3 replaces this with PAR aggregation, rollout-level credit assignment, implicit voting, reduced gradient variance, and preservation of SFT ranking structure. It also explicitly interprets the BT comparison as a trade-off and the new score trajectories as evidence against upward score drift. The limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract and reproducibility statement replace anonymous code access with a Hugging Face location advertised for code, data, and checkpoints. Conversely, Appendix C removes the description of constructing 38k pairwise examples and intersecting them with pointwise data to obtain 16.9k pairs. Other implementation, hardware, and training details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds a GPT-4.1 reference and three Zhang et al. works concerning adaptive RL sampling, thinking-mode switching, and entropy regularization. The related-work taxonomy and positioning of the core method remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the abstract, contributions, benchmark interpretation, noise discussion, and conclusion. A Best-of-N subsection is inserted, and mathematical-reasoning discussion is condensed and moved into Section 4.4. Terminology, cross-references, and the author block are also revised, while most prose and the overall structure remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 2, 17, and 18 and merges v2's mathematical-reasoning Tables 15–16 into main-text Table 4. Existing figures are unchanged. Remaining visual differences mainly involve table placement, minor formatting, and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The matched-data, matched-backbone Best-of-N comparison strengthens evidence beyond v2's downstream comparison with Skywork. Explicit acknowledgment of BT's RewardBench advantage and the new noise and score controls improve the paper's credibility. The gain is limited: Best-of-N advantages have metric-level exceptions, the controls do not directly establish the claimed variance reduction, and Appendix C loses some pairwise-data construction details.
